header.name: Probabilistic Number Theory
header.description:
This course is an introduction to the rapidly evolving field of probabilistic number theory. The underlying theme of the course is to understand the probabilistic behaviour of naturally defined arithmetic sequences, for example, the prime numbers, prime numbers in arithmetic progressions, the number of prime factors of an integer, the sum of divisors function, etc. These quantities often exhibit interesting asymptotic distribution properties. The course emphasises elementary and probabilistic methods that reveal elegant patterns in number theory.

Suitable for students with a strong interest in number theory who have completed probability, statistics, and analysis courses.

outcomes.label: CO1
outcomes.raw_text: Students will be able to identify and analyze key arithmetic functions (Möbius, prime counting, divisor functions) and compute average orders using summation techniques.

outcomes.label: CO2
outcomes.raw_text: Students will understand prime number distribution via Chebyshev functions and the prime number theorem, and apply probabilistic models to prime gaps.

outcomes.label: CO3
outcomes.raw_text: Students will compute natural, logarithmic, and analytic densities of sequences and determine limiting distributions of arithmetic functions.

outcomes.label: CO4
outcomes.raw_text: Students will apply the Erdos-Kac theorem and prove central limit theorems for arithmetic functions.

lecture_topics: Distribution of primes: Chebyshev functions, prime number theorem, probabilistic models for prime gaps
Densities of sequences: natural, logarithmic, analytic densities with examples
The Erdos-Kac theorem: number of prime factors of an integer, proof and applications
Central limit theorems in number theory

resources.title: Introduction to Analytic and Probabilistic Number Theory by Gerald Tenenbaum
An Invitation to Modern Number Theory by S. J. Miller and R. Takloo-Bighash
Probabilistic Number Theory I & II by Richard Guy
Elementary Number Theory by David M. Burton (for foundational material)
